exposure: timing of enteral nutrition initiation (within 24 hours of birth vs. after 24 hours of birth)
outcome: time to reach total enteral feeding
cohort: 2514 very premature infants born before 32 weeks of gestation from 28 hospitals in China.
finding: Early initiation of enteral feeding was associated with less frequency of feeding intolerance, extrauterine growth restriction (EUGR), and late-onset sepsis (LOS, and it may shorten the time to reach total enteral feeding without increasing the risk of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC).
